$comment: WEIGHTS-001 — the manifest git DOES hold, describing the weights git does NOT.
Rule: no binary weight ever enters this repository. Binaries are immortal in git history
and cannot be removed without rewriting it, so the only safe policy is to never add one.
This file plus scripts/fetch_weights.py is what makes a fresh machine reproducible.
`kind` tells the fetcher how to provision an entry:
hf        — huggingface_hub snapshot_download at a PINNED revision (a commit sha, never a
branch: 'main' is a moving target and would silently change which weights run)
url       — direct download to `dest`, verified against `sha256`
pip-git   — installed by requirements-ml.txt; the fetcher only reports, never installs
torch-hub — pulled by torch.hub at load time into TORCH_HOME; the fetcher pre-warms it and,
where the upstream call omits trust_repo, pre-seeds the trusted_list so a fresh
box never blocks on an interactive y/N prompt
`mirror_needed: true` marks artifacts we do NOT control and cannot re-fetch if upstream
removes them. See vault/Build/Architecture Lab/Decisions/weights-storage.md for the plan.

models.name: fashion_clip
models.size_human: 581 MB (of ~1.2 GB in the repo — the rest is ONNX we never load)
models.notes: Largest HF entry. `ignore_patterns` is load-bearing, not an optimisation: the repo ships an onnx/ variant directory that this codebase never touches (fashion_clip_service uses CLIPModel/CLIPProcessor on safetensors; nothing in backend/ imports onnx). Without it a full snapshot pulls ~600 MB of dead weight AND the cache check never passes — the local cache here has 8 abandoned .incomplete ONNX blobs from exactly that. `pytorch_model.bin` is excluded for the same reason: the repo ships both formats, transformers loads safetensors, and demanding the .bin too made every run report an IncompleteSnapshotError and re-attempt a download that would never be used.
